## The problem

Our team of twelve engineers works on long-lived feature branches, often open for two to four weeks before merging. Merge conflicts compound the longer a branch lives, so integration days routinely eat an afternoon or more. Code review happens late, against a huge diff, so reviewers skim rather than engage. And because branches diverge from main for weeks, we discover integration bugs only after merge, when they are far more expensive to fix. Release 4.2 slipped four days over a three-way merge conflict, and Release 4.3 shipped a regression that only appeared once three long-lived branches merged in the same week, none of which had been tested together.

## The proposal

I propose we adopt trunk-based development: every engineer commits to main at least once a day, using feature flags to hide incomplete work. Branches, when used at all, live under a day. This forces smaller, more reviewable changes, keeps main always releasable, and surfaces integration problems within hours instead of weeks. Two supporting steps make this workable:

- Spend one sprint building a lightweight feature-flag system and CI gating so broken commits cannot land on main.
- Run a two-week pilot with two sub-teams before a full rollout, so we can fix workflow issues at small scale first.

## What could go wrong

The strongest objection is real: trunk-based development assumes strong test coverage and fast CI, and today our suite takes eighteen minutes and has known gaps in the payments module. Switching before fixing that risks pushing broken code straight to main instead of containing it on an isolated branch, which could be worse than our current problems. I take that risk seriously rather than dismiss it: the pilot should include a payments-coverage review, and we need an agreed rollback plan, since reverting a bad commit is fast but reverting a bad long-lived merge is not.

- A smaller risk is adjustment friction: engineers used to isolated branches may feel exposed committing unfinished work to main, even behind flags, and will need a few weeks to adapt.

I would like a decision by the end of next week.
